# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 33 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_007_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 7

**1** Jesus said: "Blessed [маkаріос] is the lion [маоуe] that the human [роме] will eat and the lion will become human [роме].

**2** And cursed [охе] is the human whom the lion will eat, and the lion will become human [роме]."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- *маkаріос*: Greek loan-word; "blessed," "fortunate" — the standard beatitude form
- *маоуe*: lion; the beast
- *роме*: human being, person; the human who devours the lion transforms it
- *охе*: cursed, wretched — the antonym of *makarios*; rare in Thomas
- The saying is paradoxical and highly debated:
  - Option A: The "lion" = the bestial/passionate nature; the human who spiritually overcomes it (eats it) is blessed
  - Option B: The human who is consumed by the bestial is cursed (the lion becomes human = the passions dominate)
  - Option C: Allegorical — the worthy disciple transforms the carnal; the carnal consumed by baser nature degrades
- No Synoptic parallel; unique to Thomas
- No Greek manuscript parallel attested
